I am old, so I will not choose a management plan that is too complicated or too risky. Since I have well irrigation, I will rely on stable production rather than gambling on low-input farming. For winter wheat, I will use an improved seed, put most fertilizer at sowing with some nitrogen later, irrigate at the key stages, and keep tillage simple with rotary tillage because it is easier for me to manage on my small area. After wheat harvest, I will plant summer maize quickly on the same 10.1 mu, use hybrid seed for stronger yield, keep fertilizer moderate but enough to support grain filling, and use fewer irrigation times than wheat because the rainy season helps. I will control pests and diseases, but I will not spray excessively. My goal is steady grain yield, manageable field work, and lower production risk for my household.
